answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every result depends on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains for clones, but cannot shorten the sequential time required by any one chain; creating many identities therefore imposes repeated physical delay and compute cost. A Wesolowski proof lets others verify completion efficiently, while the tide of clone attempts still meets this per-identity bottleneck, not a lantern-lit shortcut through the vault.
